criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission, single satellite rationale, and users (operator and customers) are addressed with context and referenced background. Operator is vague (funding by university or government) and the 'Earth observation' mission is well described. Strong overall but users section is loosely specified and some claims lack citation (e.g. 'Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic' supported by a link).

evidence.quote: Coral reefs harbour some of the most diverse species of life on the planet

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Covers all listed elements but with errors: Vega E is unbuilt and launch site rationale contradicts (Kourou at 5.05N, claims two windows incorrectly), RAAN of 27.33° is unjustified, and the orbit semi-major axis and inclination are stated without the J2 derivation. Manoeuvre discussion is thin. Ground-station pass counts are given but contact duration analysis and EOL are weakly supported. Mission duration is 5 years but EOL reasoning includes garbled text. Evidence partly supported by STK screenshots.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarises the design and acknowledges the launch risk, but restates content rather than drawing detailed conclusions from the evidence (e.g. average contact times, pass counts, EOL implications). Generic in places.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and figure set, but many grammar/typo issues, a broken drag sail sentence, unlabelled/unnumbered figures and tables, a Wikipedia source explicitly disallowed, inconsistent citation style, and a contents page mismatch. Presentation falls in the adequate band.

evidence.quote: The satellite, nicknamed ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite)

technical_issues.issue: Kourou latitude 5.05°N is described as causing two launch windows per day; the rationale is confused and the claim that equatorial launches need less fuel via 'maximum rotational velocity' is loosely stated.
Stated that RAAN must change 360° per year; the sun-synchronous precession is about 0.9856°/day (~360°/year) but the text calls it a 1° daily east precession and the RAAN value 27.33° is unjustified.
Table lists semi-major axis 6971km and Argument of Latitude 0° as a fixed value, yet u changes with time; no epoch or orbital period given.
Uncontrolled re-entry at 600 km is described as burning up; at 600 km it may take decades, so the disposal claim is not supported by a lifetime calculation.
Text 'to ' and drag sail sentence are truncated; the drag sail discussion is incomplete.
Access table shows duplicated row 14 and 15 and an unnumbered row '----'; average contact claim of ~10 min matches 580 s but 15 passes listed inconsistently with the 'first fifteen' label.

overall: The report covers most required segments with STK support but has significant technical inconsistencies, unbuilt launch vehicle selection, weak justification of orbit and EOL, incomplete drag sail discussion, unlabelled figures and a disallowed Wikipedia source. Presentation and conclusion are adequate rather than strong.

feedback.summary: You have a clear, well-motivated concept: a single Earth observation satellite supporting Australian research, with the Introduction covering purpose and users well. Your STK work and ground-station access analysis give the report credible evidence. The main gaps are technical accuracy in the Launch and Orbit sections, an incomplete end-of-life discussion, presentation issues, and a disallowed Wikipedia source.
next_steps: Revise the Launch section: correct the explanation of the Kourou latitude and launch windows and the fuel argument, and justify your launch vehicle choice, given that Vega E has not yet been built. Consider naming a flying alternative.

In the Orbit section, justify your RAAN of 27.33° and correct the sun-synchronous precession description (about 0.9856° per day). Add an epoch and orbital period to the orbital elements table, and state that the argument of latitude varies with time.

Complete the Mission Duration and EOL section with a lifetime or decay calculation that supports disposal at 600 km, and finish the drag sail discussion. Replace the Wikipedia source with an authoritative reference, and label all figures and tables.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly states the primary mission, why it is needed (coral reef and ocean acidification context), and who uses the satellite. The content is detailed and referenced. To reach the top band consistently, make the operator description specific by naming the operator and funding body rather than 'university or government', and make sure every claim, such as the ocean acidification statistic, is supported by a credible cited source.
criteria.C2: You cover all the required design elements and support them with STK screenshots and pass data. Correct the Vega E launch rationale and the Kourou explanation, and justify your orbital elements, including the RAAN and inclination. Expand the manoeuvre discussion, analyse contact durations and total coverage, and back up your EOL plan with a lifetime calculation so your design choices are accurate and persuasive.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion summarises the design and openly notes the launch vehicle risk, which is a good start. To move up, draw specific conclusions from your evidence. State what the pass counts and average contact time (about 10 minutes) mean for data downlink, and what the EOL results imply for mission sustainability, rather than restating earlier sections.
criteria.C4: Your report has clear headings and a logical structure, which aids readability. Improve it by proofreading for spelling and grammar, finishing the truncated drag sail sentence, numbering and labelling every figure and table, removing the duplicated rows in the access table, aligning the contents page with the report, and using one consistent citation style with a compliant reference list.
